question: Can a later fd --exec-batch command execute before an earlier declared command when its independent command builder reaches the argv-size ceiling first?

sources.name: sharkdp/fd
sources.claim: CommandSet::execute_batch owns one CommandBuilder per declared command. Each builder independently executes finish() when its own args_would_fit check fails, so a later builder can flush while an earlier builder remains buffered.

sources.name: fd issue 2033
sources.claim: The public repeated --exec-batch contract is reported to violate declaration order when one command reaches the OS command-line limit earlier than another.

command: GitHub Actions: Fieldwork fd exec-batch order probe

dependencies: exact sharkdp/fd source fetched read-only at ee20f426ddf338ac7ead5c5f00ea49258005caaf

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: Two equal-capacity builders finish in declaration order, and making only builder 2 approach its argv ceiling still leaves command 1 as the first execution.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: Another ordering barrier defeats the source-level hypothesis; retain a negative result.

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: Equal-capacity builders execute 1 then 2, while the asymmetric-capacity case executes command 2 before command 1 once builder 2 independently flushes.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: The current batch owner has a target-executed declaration-order violation caused by independent builder flush thresholds.

stop_condition: Stop after the owner-level target test classifies independent argv-capacity flushing. If positive, design a public CLI reproduction separately before source promotion.
